issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a Stock.emptyStock() method (UML and solution define emptyStock()), but the template Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This method-name/signature mismatch is structural and can confuse students: they may implement or call emptyStock based on the specification, but the template does not define it (and the solution uses emptyStock).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the specification and solution. Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a public emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). Ensure the method name used in the problem statement, template, and solution is consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template repository's Stock class defines the same operation as clearInventory(). This inconsistency (emptyStock vs. clearInventory) refers to the same conceptual action (clearing the stock) and may confuse students when mapping the UML/specification to the provided template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier: rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or add an emptyStock() wrapper that delegates to clearInventory()) so the template matches the problem UML and the solution implementation.
